newsitem.title: KENYA: Refugees central to Great Lakes drama.
newsitem.headline: Refugees central to Great Lakes drama.

text.p: Refugees who fled to east Zaire and west Tanzania from Rwanda and Burundi, mostly in 1994, are central to the Great Lakes conflict.
Following is a list of the key populations in September this year and subsequent refugee movements based on U.N. refugee agency (UNHCR) figures.
The grand total is 1,968,000 including some new Zairean refugees fleeing fighting.

GOMA, Zaire - A total of 717,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees who fled the advancing Rwandan Patriotic Front in 1994 were housed in five giant camps around Goma in North Kivu in September. Between November 15 and 19 around 500,000 returned to Rwanda via Gisenyi after Zairean rebels shelled the camps. Around 217,000 are missing including armed Hutu extremists believed to have fled north or west deeper into Zaire. Rebels control Goma.

BUKAVU, Zaire - An estimated 307,000 Rwandan Hutus lived in 23 camps around South Kivu's regional capital Bukavu in September and almost all are still missing. The U.N's World Food Programme reported on Wednesday strong evidence that 100,000 refugees were on the move north from Bukavu, an area also controlled by Zairean rebels.

UVIRA, Zaire - A total of 225,000 Hutu refugees lived in 13 camps north of Uvira in the Rusizi delta in September of whom 144,000 were Burundian Hutus who fled Burundi's civil war and the rest Rwandan Hutus. Some 35,000 Burundians have returned home leaving around 190,000 missing. Aid officials say Rwandan Hutus from Uvira may have headed north to Bukavu, while UNHCR believes the Burundians have headed west into the hills and south.

NGARA, Tanzania - A total of 487,000 Hutus live in eight camps around Ngara of whom 410,000 are Rwandan Hutus who fled their country in 1994 and the rest Burundian Hutus. The population has remained static since September.
KARAGWE, Tanzania - A total of 123,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees from 1994 live in Karagwe camps and there has been no change in their status.

KIGOMA, Tanzania - In September around 36,000 Burundian Hutu refugees lived in Kigoma's four camps, but the population has been augmented in the past three weeks by around 48,000 Burundian refugees and 25,000 Zaireans most of whom fled across Lake Tanganyika.
